title: Compact shared histogram snapshots and indexed personal markers
status: Implemented and locally verified; not deployed

requirements.HCO01: Use sorted exact time frequencies and cumulative counts for population-independent bin queries.
requirements.HCO02: Remove unbounded per-driver dictionaries from large shared snapshots and cache loads.
requirements.HCO03: Use the owner's small-inaccuracy allowance for bounded indexed personal markers in large fields.
requirements.R01: Preserve one verified PB per driver, ties, scope isolation, visibility invalidation, leases and failed-refresh recovery.
requirements.Q01: Record executable checks, measured representation changes, source provenance and remaining acceptance.

decision.review: The original HistogramPopulation already used bisect_left over sorted distinct ticks and cumulative frequencies. Its large cost was reconstructing, persisting, transferring and caching every player's identity/time mapping. The change addresses that source of population growth and shares binary searches for neighboring bin boundaries.
decision.units: Retain exact 120 Hz canonical tick values rather than quantizing authoritative times or introducing fixed millisecond buckets. Flexible requested bin counts and retained displayed ranges continue to work; the existing client already handles tail display and comparison range continuity.
decision.precomputation: Public race distributions reuse the existing transactionally maintained BoardTimeCount frequencies. Flying-lap and combined real/development distributions are grouped and deduplicated in SQL during background refresh. Only distinct tick counts leave SQL for large fields.
decision.write_cost: No new per-race database writes, shared counters, migrations or external dependencies were introduced by this task. Fully incremental flying-lap/cross-board comparison projections were deliberately not added to race finalization.
decision.small_fields: At up to 4096 drivers, frozen per-player snapshot values remain exact. The personal-map SQL fetch also has a hard LIMIT of 4097 and discards overflow.
decision.large_fields: Larger fields omit personal maps and look up only the requesting player's current race/lap PB by indexed player ID. comparison_approximate=true explicitly marks this path. Compared with removing that player's original snapshot contribution, self-correction can differ by at most one rank place and the population denominator by one. Existing snapshot refresh lag can additionally reflect newer accepted results. No records, rewards or competitive ranks are approximated.
decision.legacy: Large legacy payloads are read using only JSON frequency/grid projections, excluding their old personal maps. They remain usable before an ordinary changed-revision refresh rewrites them as format 2. PostgreSQL may still parse/toast legacy JSON on a cold load; this is a transitional database cost, not a population-independent claim for old stored JSON.
decision.rolling_readers: Format 2 keeps own={} plus own_mode=indexed in compact fields. The preserved original loader was executed against the new ten-million weighted payload and successfully read its distribution. Older readers can temporarily omit the personal marker until updated, rather than failing to decode it.

behavior: from_frequencies builds cumulative arrays without expanding weighted samples into driver rows.
B requested bins use B+1 binary searches over U sorted distinct tick values: O(B log U). A compatible default stored grid remains precomputed.
Compact snapshot storage and cold Python allocation depend on U plus the fixed small-map cap, rather than driver population. Legitimate tick values are bounded by the replay tick domain.
Two metadata/payload reads are generation-fenced. Claim/publication queries defer payload loading, including for large legacy snapshots.
Warm snapshot caching keeps the original four-entry and 128 MiB estimated-weight budgets; omitted personal maps no longer evict otherwise-small large-population snapshots.
Personal filters are applied before race grouping and inside public/private flying-lap queries. Existing artificial cutoff, public/test deduplication and visibility rules remain.
Display-only candidates never add samples or alter shared counts. Rank endpoints are clamped safely when the current PB is newer than the distribution.

measurements.scope: Synthetic Python representation benchmark using the preserved original class and 1000 distinct time ticks; not HTTP/database/deployment throughput.

10000000_weighted_drivers.qualification: Weighted counts, not ten million seeded players or accepted races.

actual_http_handler.qualification: Actual in-process FastAPI HTTP request over a synthetic ten-million-driver stored snapshot. Only its creator is a normal verified fixture account; the other counts are weighted synthetic data.

measurements.timing_qualification: These local representation timings were sampled while other local tests could run; sizes, count conservation and cache admission are the main evidence. No deployment speedup or throughput claim.

Concurrent reward/queue changes are not authored or claimed by this task.
